hypothesis: cuBLAS tiles about 128 rows of N, so small-M projections launch only N/128 CTAs (qkv N=2304 is about 18) and leave most of the H200's 132 SMs idle. Splitting K across an N-tile of 64 until the grid is about 2*132 CTAs, with each BF16 weight read once through 16-byte streaming loads, should cut small-M time. m>32 stays on the starter matmul so verify loads are not exposed to a custom large-M kernel.
fast_path: CUDA is available and m<=32 and n%64==0 and k%64==0. One CTA owns 64 N-rows and one K-split; threads stream float4 weights with __ldcs, stage the activation tile, and accumulate FP32. A second kernel reduces partials along K and stores BF16, or FP32 for the router. Router weights stay FP32 (BF16 activations are promoted). The partial workspace is allocated in prepare for m<=32, n<=8192, and up to 64 splits.
fallback: Starter math: BF16 is x @ W[:config.n].T and the router is x.float() @ W[:config.n].T. Used when CUDA is unavailable, m>32, or n or k is not a multiple of 64.
reject_if: CPU smoke fails, m>32 disagrees with the starter matmul, router error exceeds 1e-4 or a probe row exceeds 1e-3, or the fast path syncs or allocates in a way that breaks CUDA graph replay.
